messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT created (KV_CACHE_GROWTH) 2459123456 — cluster eu-west-1-gpu-pool-7. Continuous-batcher pack queues growing, paging rate up, token latency p95 spike. Auto-escalating to oncall.

Alice H: ack, I'm on it. grabbing traces and query plans.

Ben K (oncall): I'm paged. Patch owner is eng-runtime — looping in Carmen and Lucy. Anyone seeing immediate customer errors?

Rahul (CS): saw a couple of customer reports around 12:08 UTC of slow responses and some 429s. I'll compile exact IDs. No PagerDuty customer pages yet.

Carmen R: quick summary from initial triage: after last week's packer tuning, aggressive KV prefetch combined with mixed long/short requests is causing pack growth to blow up. Continuous batching packs grow unbounded when a small percentage of long sequences join the pack. When pack memory crosses paging threshold, we get heavy page-in latency and the batcher effectively starves short requests.

Lucy M: past 10m logs:
```
[12:07:14] batcher: pack_create id=0x7f3 len=1 items=1 mem=4.2MB
[12:07:19] packer: prefetch key=K:usr:1234 size=2.1MB
[12:07:20] batcher: pack_append id=0x7f3 items=37 mem=320MB
[12:07:21] kernel: swapin 320MB -> paging spike latency=1.4s
[12:07:22] batcher: short_request latency p95=2.1s p99=6.9s
```
Looks like pack sizes ramped from <64->>300 items in seconds.

Ben K: immediate mitigation proposal:
- disable aggressive prefetch
- lower max_pack_items and max_pack_age to bound pack size
- throttle prefetch budget per inst
Apply as a config hotfix and roll to canary.

Ben K: hotfix payload (applied to cluster config API):
```
PATCH /internal/v1/configs/batcher
{
  "continuous_batching.max_pack_items": "64",
  "continuous_batching.max_pack_age_ms": "10",
  "continuous_batching.enable_aggressive_prefetch": "false",
  "continuous_batching.kv_prefetch_budget": "0.10"
}
```

Ben K: deploy steps:
1) push config to canary (10%)
2) monitor p95/p99 + paging rate for 5m
3) if good, roll to 100%

deploy-bot: canary rollout started -> 10% (eu-west-1-gpu-pool-7-canary)

Alice H: applying canary now.

deploy-bot: canary rollout complete -> 10% success

Lucy M: monitoring --- after canary p95 for short requests dropped 2.1s -> 480ms, p99 6.9s -> 1.2s. Paging rate dropped ~78% in the canary nodes. No increase in error rate.

Carmen R: good sign. I recommend immediate full roll after 10m stable window. Also we should add a quick pack-size guard in runtime to avoid unbounded pack growth while we redesign scheduler fairness.

Ben K: rolling to 100% now.

deploy-bot: rollout progressing -> 50% -> 100% complete

deploy-bot: rollout finished: 100% applied

Alice H: post-roll metrics: cluster p95 0.5s, p99 1.25s, paging IOPS back to baseline. Short-request tail latency normalized.

Rahul (CS): customer impact summary for status update:
- Affected customers: 12 customer orgs saw >1s latency between 12:06-12:20 UTC.
- Two customers saw 429 throttles when their retries hit rate-limits during the spike.
- No data loss. All requests eventually completed.
I'll prepare a brief status note and notify impacted accounts.

Seema P: assigning post-incident tasks: we need a postmortem, timeline, and action items. Owner: Lucy M. Add ticket for scheduler fairness work and e2e tests for mixed workloads.

Jordan (PM): high priority: we need to surface this to product and evaluate if packer tuning defaults should be more conservative for multi-tenant clusters. Also need clear comms to enterprise customers.

Dave L: observed scheduler fairness issue: when large requests are entering packs, packer tends to prefer packing and delaying small requests (packing amortization wins) — effectively starves short latency-sensitive requests. Short-term fix: add small-request priority or cap per-packer large-item ratio.

Carmen R: agreed. Proposed medium-term fixes:
- add adaptive packing: if average pack_items > N, favor small items for next M packs
- add KV-prefetch budget enforcement per request-class
- add pack eviction watermark to gently flush large packs before paging

Lucy M: I'll own the follow-up CLs. I'll open two PRs:
1) runtime: pack-size sentinel & eviction (tests + perf)
2) scheduler: small-request bias + regression tests using mixed-shapes harness

Ben K: handoff — I'm off in 55m. Handoff to Dave L for remaining verification and postmortem tracking. @Dave L please ack.

Dave L: acked. I'll take next-oncall. Will coordinate postmortem and blameless RCA.

Rahul (CS): drafting customer note now; will send short workaround update ("we deployed a config fix to limit batching/prefetch which reduced latencies; we will follow up with a permanent fix and postmortem").

incidents-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED 2459123809 — root-cause: regressive packer prefetch + mixed workload causing unbounded pack growth -> paging -> batcher starvation. Mitigation: config hotfix (disabled aggressive prefetch, bounded pack size) rolled to 100% at 2459123690. Monitoring stable 30m.

Seema P: postmortem owner Lucy M. Please include timeline, customer impact, code/infra changes, and follow-up ETA for scheduler fairness CLs.

Lucy M: will send initial postmortem draft by EOD. Follow-ups: scheduler CLs targeted for next sprint, add e2e mixed-shape test to perf harness.

Jordan (PM): thanks team. Rahul, ping me when customer note is ready.

Ben K: :thumbsup: great work all. Closing thread after postmortem link.

(reacts: many :thumbsup: and :eyes:)
